_comment: Path template. Two placeholders are substituted at run time by run_pipeline.py:
{PKG}    -> this package's root (code/bin/config that you copy between servers)
{ASSETS} -> the big data bundle (databases + checkpoints + backbone), set in site.json
Do not edit paths here for a new server -- edit config/site.json instead.
parent_evidence: how a domain's genus/phylum evidence is produced. NOT interchangeable --
'rollup' aggregates upward from the top-20 species (bacteria, fungi: verified bit-identical);
'direct' queries a per-rank index (virus: its DB is direct-rank; a rollup provably cannot
reproduce it). The DL for each domain was trained on the evidence its mode produces.
threshold: deployment pins a fixed gate threshold tau=0.5 (real reads have no known error rate).

l1_routing._chunk_size_note: reads processed in this many rows per step48 invocation (run_p1_route_chunked.sh) so p1 RAM = one chunk + the ~90G compact DB, not the whole sample. Lower it if p1 still OOMs on very deep samples.
l1_routing._calls: best==0 -> no_call ; tied max -> ambiguous ; else the domain, status=called
l1_routing._human_note: human reads are routed but NOT classified further -- there is no human DL model.

_query_binary_note: query_binary = original mphf_query_fast (still used for the VIRUS parent evidence, which needs --mask-shape parent -- the multi binary does not implement that). query_binary_multi = mphf_query_fast_multi (load-once + --chunk-size + --jobs), used for the species evidence where the 380G bacteria index makes load-once/chunking matter; byte-identical to the original (verified by cmp). k25_chunk_size caps reads-in-RAM per chunk so bacteria k25 stays under a 500G node.

resources._note: Per-stage Slurm resources (SLURM mode only; ignored on standalone). Right-sized from real history (narval pitfalls 8.5): keep bacteria k25 mem UNDER a cluster memory tier (490G fits the abundant ~498/500G tier; 560G was forced onto the scarce ~2TB tier). Tune per cluster with `sinfo -o '%P %l %m %c'`.

bacteria._resources: the 380 GB index needs ~500 GB RAM; load it once per run, not per chunk
